title: Implement Soft Delete
question: Design and implement soft delete functionality. Requirements: 1) Entities should be marked as deleted instead of physical deletion, 2) Queries should automatically exclude deleted entities, 3) Admin endpoints to view/restore deleted entities, 4) Cascade soft delete to child entities, 5) Audit trail of deletions. Discuss: adding 'deleted' boolean or 'deletedAt' timestamp field to entities, using @Where(clause = "deleted = false") on entity class to filter deleted records automatically, implementing @SQLDelete annotation to override default delete behavior with UPDATE statement, creating custom repository methods to include deleted entities when needed, using @PreRemove lifecycle callback to set deletion fields, implementing soft delete cascade by marking child entities as deleted in parent's @PreRemove, creating audit fields (@CreatedBy, @DeletedBy) using AuditorAware, implementing restore functionality by updating deleted flag, using @Filter with @FilterDef for dynamic filtering of deleted entities, handling unique constraints with deleted entities (add deleted flag to unique index), considering performance impact of filtering deleted records, and testing soft delete behavior.

title: Comprehensive Audit Logging
question: Design a comprehensive audit logging system for database changes. Requirements: 1) Track all CRUD operations, 2) Store before/after values, 3) Capture user information, 4) Timestamp all changes, 5) Query audit history, 6) Minimal performance impact. Discuss: using Hibernate Envers for automatic entity versioning, annotating entities with @Audited to enable auditing, configuring audit table naming strategy, implementing custom RevisionEntity to store user information, using @RevisionTimestamp and @RevisionNumber for tracking, implementing selective auditing with @Audited(targetAuditMode = RelationTargetAuditMode.NOT_AUDITED), creating queries to retrieve entity history using AuditReader, implementing custom @NotAudited for sensitive fields, storing audit data in separate schema/database for scalability, implementing audit data retention policies, using @Modifying attributes to control what gets audited, creating audit reports and APIs, considering async audit log writing for performance, and testing audit completeness.

title: Multi-Tenancy Data Isolation
question: Implement multi-tenancy with data isolation. Requirements: 1) Separate data per tenant, 2) Tenant identification from request context, 3) Automatic tenant filtering in queries, 4) Support for shared and tenant-specific entities, 5) Schema per tenant OR discriminator column approach. Discuss: choosing between separate database per tenant, separate schema per tenant, or shared schema with discriminator column, implementing TenantIdentifierResolver to resolve current tenant from ThreadLocal, using MultiTenantConnectionProvider for separate datasources per tenant, adding tenant_id column to all tenant-specific entities, using @Filter with @FilterDef to automatically add tenant filtering to queries, implementing @TenantId annotation (Hibernate 6.0+) for automatic tenant handling, storing tenant context in ThreadLocal via servlet filter/interceptor, implementing tenant-aware repositories, handling tenant switching for admin operations, using separate EntityManagerFactory per tenant for complete isolation, implementing tenant provisioning and cleanup, preventing cross-tenant data access with integration tests, and optimizing connection pooling for multi-tenant scenarios.

title: Handling Concurrent Updates
question: Design a system to handle concurrent updates gracefully. Requirements: 1) Detect concurrent modifications, 2) Provide user-friendly conflict resolution, 3) Prevent lost updates, 4) Support merge strategies, 5) Audit conflict resolutions. Discuss: using @Version annotation for optimistic locking, catching OptimisticLockException in global exception handler, returning 409 Conflict with current entity state to client, implementing three-way merge (original, client version, server version), providing conflict resolution UI showing differences, implementing automatic merge strategies (last write wins, field-level merge), using @OptimisticLocking(type = OptimisticLockType.DIRTY) for field-level versioning, implementing retry logic with exponential backoff for transient conflicts, storing conflict resolution history for audit, using ETags in REST API for optimistic concurrency control, implementing pessimistic locking for critical sections, providing manual conflict resolution workflows, monitoring conflict rates as business metric, and testing concurrent modification scenarios.

title: Dynamic Search with Complex Filters
question: Implement dynamic search with complex filtering capabilities. Requirements: 1) Support multiple filter criteria, 2) AND/OR logic combinations, 3) Range queries, 4) IN queries, 5) Type-safe query construction, 6) Performance optimization. Discuss: using Specification<T> interface for dynamic query building, implementing Specification methods for each filter criteria, using CriteriaBuilder for constructing predicates, combining Specifications using and(), or(), not() methods, implementing custom SearchCriteria DTO with operation (equals, like, gt, lt, in), parsing filter string like "name:like:john,age:gt:25" into specifications, using JpaSpecificationExecutor in repository interface, implementing generic filter parser for reusable search, using @EntityGraph to prevent N+1 queries, adding pagination and sorting to search results, implementing QueryDSL for more complex type-safe queries, creating indexed views for frequently searched columns, caching search results for popular queries, and testing search performance with large datasets.

title: Optimize Batch Processing
question: Optimize batch insert/update of millions of records. Requirements: 1) Process millions of records, 2) Minimize memory usage, 3) Handle failures gracefully, 4) Progress tracking, 5) Resume capability. Discuss: using StatelessSession for batch operations to bypass first-level cache, configuring JDBC batch size (hibernate.jdbc.batch_size=50), using hibernate.order_inserts and hibernate.order_updates for better batching, disabling second-level cache during batch operations, flushing and clearing EntityManager periodically (every 50 records), using scrollable results for reading large datasets, implementing chunk-based processing with Spring Batch, using native batch inserts via JDBC template for maximum performance, implementing savepoints for batch rollback, tracking progress with batch counters, storing failed records in error table for retry, using parallel processing with partitioning, optimizing database with disabled triggers/constraints during batch load, implementing idempotency for restart capability, monitoring heap memory and batch execution time, and testing with production-size datasets.

title: Read-Write Database Splitting
question: Implement read-write database splitting for scalability. Requirements: 1) Route writes to master, reads to replicas, 2) Automatic failover, 3) Handle replication lag, 4) Transaction routing, 5) Dynamic replica discovery. Discuss: using AbstractRoutingDataSource to route queries to different datasources, implementing custom DataSource router based on transaction mode (@Transactional(readOnly=true)), using ThreadLocal to store routing key, configuring multiple datasources (master, replica1, replica2) in properties, implementing @ReadOnly custom annotation for explicit read routing, using AOP to intercept method calls and set routing context, implementing load balancing across multiple read replicas, handling replication lag by reading from master after writes (session stickiness), implementing circuit breaker for failed replicas, using @TransactionalEventListener(phase = AFTER_COMMIT) for eventual consistency, monitoring replication lag between master and replicas, implementing automatic failover with replica promotion, testing split configuration in production-like environment, and measuring performance improvement.

title: Store and Query Hierarchical Data
question: Design storage and querying of hierarchical data (tree structures). Requirements: 1) Store organization hierarchy, 2) Query all descendants, 3) Query path to root, 4) Move subtrees, 5) Efficient queries. Discuss: choosing between adjacency list (parent_id), nested sets, or closure table approaches, implementing self-referential @ManyToOne relationship for adjacency list, using recursive CTEs for querying all descendants in SQL, implementing @Where annotation to exclude soft-deleted nodes, using @Formula for computed path field, implementing move operation with consistency checks, using nested set model for read-heavy workloads (left, right boundaries), implementing closure table pattern for flexible queries, caching frequently accessed subtrees, using @BatchSize for optimizing lazy loading of children, implementing breadth-first and depth-first traversal, handling cyclic references prevention, using @OrderColumn for maintaining child order, and testing large hierarchies performance.
